Simulator incident-001: pgbouncer in prod has elevated latency. The status and diagnostic-log tools can provide evidence. In this toy environment a restart clears the connection pool, but inspection does not.

{"tool": "read_diagnostic_logs", "simulated": true, "evidence_id": "log-001", "observations": ["Backend database health check succeeds.", "All 100 pool slots are occupied by stalled sessions.", "New client requests time out waiting for a pool slot."]}

Simulated incident-001 indicates that the pgbouncer service in the prod namespace is experiencing a "pool_exhausted" state. This means that all available slots in the connection pool are occupied by stalled sessions, preventing new client requests from being served. The diagnostic logs confirm that all 100 pool slots are in use, and new client requests are timing out due to the lack of available slots.

Given this information, it appears that the issue is not with the service itself but rather with the stalled sessions in the pool. Restarting the service would not resolve this issue as it would clear the current pool state but not address the underlying problem of the stalled sessions.

The recommended next step is to investigate why the sessions are stalled and to attempt to revive them. This could involve checking the backend database health, ensuring that it is not the cause of the stalled sessions, and possibly using a command to revive the sessions. 

I will submit this diagnosis to P17 for further action.
